notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (data.js fy 'Dec 2024'). The source is Samsung Electronics' English '2024 Business Report' (K-IFRS, file name 2024_4Q_Interim_Report.pdf), hosted on Samsung's own CDN (images.samsung.com) and linked from samsung.com/global/ir. Figures in millions of KRW converted to billions. RELATION: 'founding-family' is used. The report lists Lee Jae-yong as a 'Related party of the major shareholder' (Samsung Life Insurance), as is Ra-hee Hong; he is not a registered director in the report. OWNERSHIP BASIS: all percentages are as stated in the report and are percentages of common (voting) shares issued, including treasury shares; preferred stakes are percentages of the preferred class. Nothing is recomputed. Lee also holds 137,757 preferred shares (0.02% of preferred), not included in his 1.63%. The report gives no percentage of all shares (common plus preferred), and pctVoting is left null because the report gives a stake of common shares, not voting power. Lee's main economic exposure is indirect, as Samsung C&T's 19.06% major shareholder, and that is not added. FAMILY: the 20.07% related-party total already includes Lee's own 1.63% along with Samsung Life Insurance (8.51% + 0.09% special accounts), Samsung C&T (5.01%), Samsung Fire & Marine (1.49%), Samsung foundations, Ra-hee Hong (1.64%), Boo-jin Lee (0.80%), Seo-hyun Lee (0.79%) and affiliate executives. Samsung Life and Samsung C&T, though over 5% each, are therefore not listed as separate holders. BLACKROCK: very stale. Samsung bases it on a February 7, 2019 mass-holding report (holdings as of January 28, 2019). DIVIDENDS: the consolidated cash-flow 'Dividends paid' of KRW 10,888,749m includes dividends paid by subsidiaries to non-controlling interests (the consolidated equity statement shows KRW 1,102,625m declared to non-controlling interests in 2024). The parent company's separate cash-flow line (KRW 9,808,653m) is used as the cash paid to Samsung Electronics' own shareholders. It covers common and preferred shareholders together. BUYBACKS: 'Treasury shares purchased' is the same KRW 1,811,775m in the consolidated and separate statements; the report says the Board resolved on November 15, 2024 to repurchase shares and that 'the Company repurchased 3 trillion won out of the 10 trillion won worth of shares and then cancelled the acquired shares in February 2025.' STOCK COMP is null: the FY2024 statements show no share-based payment expense, and no stock options were outstanding for registered directors. The report says a stock-based compensation system (restricted shares for executives' OPI bonus) was implemented in January 2025, with grants in January 2026. That is after this fiscal year and covers executives only, so no plan is recorded. GEOGRAPHY: Samsung's five regions as reported to its Management Committee.

footprint.notes: Employees by region from the Sustainability Report 2025 (2024 column; the quoted rows also show 2022 and 2023). The Korea row is the only single-country figure; the other regions are Samsung's own groupings (Asia covers Southeast Asia, Southwest Asia, China and Japan) and no country list is given, so countries is null for them. Regional rows sum to the company total of 262,647; they exclude 59,693 non-Samsung Electronics workers reported separately. Samsung says it owns 240 manufacturing sites, sales offices, R&D centers and design centers in total, 33 of them manufacturing sites (Sustainability Report 2025), but no per-country site count. The Business Report names major production sites by product: smartphones at Gumi (plus Vietnam, India and Brazil) and memory at Hwaseong, Pyeongtaek and other Korean sites plus China. Sites come from the FY2024 Business Report (company-hosted English translation of the DART filing); the Taylor, Texas foundry is recorded only as the 2021 investment announcement the report describes. Taxes: Samsung publishes the regional split of taxes and public duties (2024: Korea 36.6%, Americas and Europe 40.7%, Asia 21.2%, others 1.5% of KRW 8.2 trillion); those tax regions are a different grouping from the employee regions and are listed as separate rows. No U.S. state data.
